text:
maria: Quick check — we're getting a couple support tickets where requests without X-Project-ID succeed for some keys but fail for others. Are we intentionally inferring project from org-key fallback?
kevin: Not intentionally — server should require explicit project when a key is project-scoped. If key is org-scoped, we allow missing X-Project-ID and route to default project behavior.
arnav: This is the tricky bit: during key rotation some keys are temporarily promoted to org-scope for compatibility. Need to know exact precedence.
maria: Right — the question from support: client used an older key (project-scoped) but X-Project-ID was omitted; why did it succeed once?
kevin: Two possibilities: 1) there was a cached auth mapping from the previous org-key check, or 2) the request hit a node still running the older compatibility flag.
arnav: We have a short grace period after rotation (10m) where we accept either project or org header to avoid breaking clients. That was added last quarter, maybe not well-documented.
jess: Security note — if we accept missing project header based on grace/implied fallback we must log the fallback event and emit an audit entry. Compliance teams will want visibility.
maria: Good call, we should surface that in console and billing to avoid attribution issues. Also: what should SDK do? Auto-infer project from config?
kevin: SDK should not "infer" silently. It can provide a convenience that warns locally if X-Project-ID missing and the API key is org-scoped, but server decisions must be explicit.
arnav: Proposed behaviour for server: precedence = explicit X-Project-ID > project-scoped key binding > org-scoped key fallback. If key rotation in progress, allow org-scoped fallback for up to 10m and log event. Return 403 when auth is valid but project doesn't have access; return 401 when key invalid/expired.
maria: Can we standardize error bodies? Support requests show different messages. Example we should use: 401 -> {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key invalid or expired"} ; 403 -> {"error":"forbidden","message":"project access denied"} 
kevin: Yes. Also include an optional "fallback_used": "org_fallback" boolean in debug headers for internal tracing (only in prod logs, not returned to public).
jess: If we add fallback flag to headers returned in the response for internal customers (dedicated/private) that might be acceptable. Public hosted API should not expose fallback details to end-users.
maria: Tests: arnav, can you add unit tests for header precedence and an integration test simulating rotation window? Also a quick e2e using curl: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_org_OLD..." -H "Accept: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
arnav: Yup. I'll add tests that assert 401 vs 403 messages and that audit log entries include "org_fallback" when applicable.
kevin: One more: SDKs should surface a non-fatal warning when they detect missing X-Project-ID and the key in config is org scoped. Eg: console.warn("Missing X-Project-ID; using org-scoped key; set project to avoid fallback");
maria: Sounds good. I'll update the support KB with exact error strings and the 10m rotation grace note.
jess: I'll open a compliance ticket to ensure fallback events are retained for 90 days.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for auth-service v2.14.3 — routing flag for rotation-grace enabled. Rollout: 5% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m. :robot_face:
arnav: Thx — will run integration tests against canary and report failures in this thread.
maria: Thanks everyone. Action items: arnav add tests + CI job, kevin publish error spec snippet in docs, jess file retention ticket, maria update support KB. Ping here when canary passes. :white_check_mark:
